clue.text: It's a job for company boss to get in old car, step on it

definitions.text: It's a job for company boss
definitions.meaning: a managing director's task is to run the board of directors

definitions.text: to get in old car, step on it
definitions.meaning: the footboard along the side of a vintage car that you stand on to climb in

explanation.surface: A busy executive is told to climb into a vintage car and floor the accelerator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'step on it' sounds like an order to hurry, but it names the step itself; read the first half as two words, running + board, what a chief executive does.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the work of chairing directors, and also the name for the side step on old cars.

clue.text: Kick off again with skill after half-time?

indicators.note: skill comes after the half-time break, so its letters follow

parts.note: the interval in a football match is a rest for the players
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A football team resumes play after the interval with more flair.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick off again is to begin play once more, a synonym for starting afresh.

clue.text: I will cut inferior? Not at all

indicators.note: the I will cut into the other word, sitting inside it

parts.note: nether means lower, as in the nether regions

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they may slash an inferior thing, and the reply is 'not at all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used in reply, the word means not one or the other, a firm refusal of both.

clue.text: Spruce woman goes after fashionable hospital

parts.note: in means in fashion
a spruce is a kind of fir tree
Mary is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed woman follows a trendy hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spruce' looks like an adjective, smart, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: An infirmary is a traditional name for a hospital, especially in British towns.

clue.text: Great upmarket chic clothing is primarily supplied here

definitions.text: Great upmarket chic clothing is primarily supplied here

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so take the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A luxury fashion house is where great upmarket chic clothing comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian luxury label sells designer clothes, so the whole clue describes the brand.

clue.text: Word I had after opponent initially made optimistic call at bridge

indicators.note: the word and I had follow the opponent's first letter
initially picks out the opening letter of opponent

parts.note: a verb is a word, a part of speech
I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: A bridge player explains bidding high after the opposition opened.
explanation.definitionFit: To bid more than the cards can make is an optimistic call in the card game bridge.

clue.text: Tail err badly in second test

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of the two words are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A tail that errs badly in a second examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A court hearing a case again tests the evidence a second time.

clue.text: These help to bring round humming sailors

parts.note: humming is British slang for smelling strongly
salts, as in old salts, are experienced sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors humming a tune help bring a ship round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humming' looks like singing; in British slang it means stinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia-based salts were sniffed to revive someone who had fainted, bringing them round.

clue.text: Funny men, twin heroes not around

indicators.note: around signals the letters of the three words are moved about

explanation.surface: Comedians, twin heroes, are not present.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TWO RONNIES was a long-running BBC comedy show starring Ronnie Barker and Ronnie Corbett.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronnie Barker and Ronnie Corbett were a famous British comedy double act, so funny men.

clue.text: Fierce creature, the old woman's having argument

parts.note: the old woman is a slang name for mother, ma, with its possessive
a tiff is a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: A savage beast belonging to an old woman is the subject of a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large powerful guard dog, an example of a fierce animal.

clue.text: Fast runner, one using unfair methods by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for the dishonest person is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: someone who uses unfair methods is a cheater

explanation.surface: A sprinter seems to be winning by foul means.
explanation.definitionFit: The big cat is the fastest land animal, a sprinter of the savannah.

clue.text: Hide article held by King

indicators.note: the article is held inside the king's name

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A king keeps an item hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb but is the noun, an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal skin, and tanned it becomes the material used for shoes and bags.

clue.text: One Butlin's resort could be integral

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Butlin is the name, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A single Butlin's holiday resort might be part of the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: Butlin's is a chain of British holiday camps, so 'resort' looks like a noun; it is the rearranging verb, re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built in is an integral, fixed part of the structure.

clue.text: Bury Football Club

definitions.meaning: to bury a body is to lay it in a grave
Internazionale of Milan is commonly known by its short name

explanation.surface: Bury Football Club, an English lower-league team.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester with a football club, so the clue reads as one team's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay to rest in a grave, and also the short name of the Milan side Internazionale.

clue.text: Timid beast — roam about, nibbling a herb

indicators.note: the rearranged letters nibble the a and herb, holding them inside
about signals the letters of roam are moved around

parts.note: dill is a feathery herb

explanation.surface: A shy animal wanders about, munching a herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges the letters of roam into ARMO, which goes round the a and the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: The armoured mammal curls into a ball when threatened, a shy and timid creature.

clue.text: Spread grain indiscriminately for horse to eat

indicators.note: the horse eats the mixed letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: scattered indiscriminately, the letters of grain are mixed up

explanation.surface: Scattering grain carelessly for a horse to feed on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb about scattering grain; it is the noun, something for bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute, spread on bread or toast.

clue.text: One denies advantage writer of detective stories detailed

parts.note: a gain is an advantage or benefit

indicators.note: de-tailed means with the tail removed, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels

explanation.surface: A crime novelist with an edge has had her stories set out in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict, so one who gainsays is a denier.

clue.text: Account given by word of mouth

definitions.meaning: a bill sent for goods or services is an account
... means sung or spoken out loud

explanation.surface: A story told orally rather than written down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second sense as two words, in voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill listing charges is an account sent to a customer for payment.

clue.text: South American resistance eat fish

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: A South American resistance movement eats fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily fish of the herring family, often tinned.

clue.text: Political commentator's endless sauce

indicators.note: endless means without the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Robert Peston is a British political journalist and broadcaster

explanation.surface: A political pundit's interminable cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sauce' could mean cheek, fitting a pundit; here it is the basil one. Robert PESTON is a well-known British TV political editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian basil, pine-nut and cheese condiment for pasta.

clue.text: Stolid trap for criminals in mission abroad

parts.note: po, as in po-faced, means solemn and unexpressive
a sting is a police operation to trap criminals

explanation.surface: An unimaginative trap for crooks overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat's or soldier's posting is an assignment to a station overseas.

clue.text: It stops leaks from Bennett in television

indicators.note: Bennett's first name goes in the word for television

parts.note: a television is a set
Alan Bennett is an English playwright

explanation.surface: The playwright Alan Bennett appears on TV to stop leaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is a substance applied to joints to make them watertight.

clue.text: Unfavourable jingle, apparently

definitions.meaning: an advertising jingle is a verse for an advertisement

explanation.surface: A jingle seems to go down badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the second sense as ad verse, a rhyme for a commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions are hostile or harmful, the opposite of favourable.

clue.text: Chapter in uplifting story draws applause

indicators.note: the chapter letter goes in the turned word
in a down clue uplifting means the word is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A chapter in a heartening story wins applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns TALE into ELAT, which takes C.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is a showy success or burst of acclaim, from French for brilliance.

clue.text: Having a ban sit out and take no part

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the three words are put out of order

explanation.surface: Under a ban, someone sits a game out rather than joining in.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from voting or joining in, declining to participate.

clue.text: Easy time: I will get entertained by competitor

indicators.note: the I will be entertained, held inside the competitor

parts.note: a rival is a competitor

explanation.surface: Someone expects a relaxed time being hosted by a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slight and unimportant is easy, a minor matter needing no effort.

clue.text: International university in America scoffed finding fake

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
scoffed is British slang for ate greedily

explanation.surface: An international university in America mocked a forgery it found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffed' looks like mocked; here it is the British sense of eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To fake something is to copy or mimic it, a synonym in the verb sense.

clue.text: Record number seeing TV they turned off

indicators.note: turned off signals the letters of the three words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Viewers switched off a record number of televisions.
explanation.walkthrough: A 78 is an old shellac gramophone record played at 78 rpm; the answer is also a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Old gramophone discs spun at 78 rpm were called by that number.
